text:
**Legionella incident, Building C cooling tower (resolved, one decision needed)**

I am writing to provide an update on the Legionella incident at the Building C cooling tower. The incident is now resolved, although one decision is needed from you, which I set out below. To begin with, a routine test conducted on 29 September found Legionella at a level of 1,200 CFU/mL. In response, we notified the health department within 24 hours, and we then disinfected and cleaned the tower. After a resample taken on 9 October showed no detection, we returned the tower to service. I can also confirm that no illness has been linked to the site.

Turning to the cause, the incident was traced to a failed biocide dosing pump. The contractor had visited monthly and missed this fault during those visits, and we were not informed of it at the time. The pump has since been replaced. To prevent a recurrence of this kind of oversight, the contractor must now confirm each visit in writing and report any missed visit.

Finally, on costs, the total comes to $7,350, and we plan to recover this amount from the contractor. **Decision needed: approve $4,800 for a dosing pump alarm.** Until that alarm is installed, weekly manual checks are in place to cover the gap. We appreciate your attention to this matter and are happy to provide further details if needed.
